claim: Biomimicry designs solutions by emulating patterns strategies and structures found in nature
Universal design creates products and environments usable by all people to the greatest extent possible without adaptation
The Bauhaus school founded in 1919 unified art craft and technology influencing modern architecture and industrial design
Geodesic domes distribute structural stress evenly across their surface allowing large spans with minimal material
Vernacular architecture uses local materials and traditions adapted to climate and culture rather than imported styles
Green building certification systems like LEED and BREEAM evaluate environmental performance of buildings across multiple criteria
Parametric design uses algorithms to generate complex forms that respond to environmental and structural constraints
Mass timber construction using cross-laminated timber sequesters carbon and can replace concrete and steel in mid-rise buildings
Biophilic design incorporates natural elements like daylight plants and water features to improve occupant health and productivity
The circular economy in construction aims to design buildings for disassembly so materials can be reused at end of life
